    - Hm? Oh, hello, *Player*. Sorry. I was writing down a heckle from three sessions ago that I only just understood. It was very good. Sit, if you like. Do not sit on the minutes.
    - One night. The Table agreed in one night. I have been through every shelf: the fastest yes in forty years, and the last one was about a goat. I have underlined it twice. I never underline twice.
    - Look at this black. Look at it. Octopus ink, *Player*, your octopus ink, and it sits on the page like it means it. I have copied eleven pages this week instead of three.
    - Ozzie came by this morning to argue about the goat vote. He was so happy he forgot to look for his spectacles for an entire hour. You did that. I have written it down.
    - Something for the record?
        - *Choice:* What do you write down?
        - *Choice:* Why do they call you Inkpot?
        - *Choice:* Tell me about the oldest books.
        - *Choice:* How often does Bastian change his mind?
        - *Choice:* Nothing, thanks.
    - Everything. Every motion, every vote, every speech, every heckle, every joke. Especially the jokes. The decisions are only half of what the Table is. The other half is how it got there, and that half is mostly jokes.
    - If somebody says the Table agreed to a thing nine years ago, I go to the shelves and find out whether it did. It usually did not. People remember the Table the way they wish it had gone.
    - Years ago a guild master from Selsior visited the Table, to see what all the noise was about. He leaned over my desk to read the minutes. Everyone leans on the desk. And the inkpot went over, all down his good blue coat.
    - I minuted it. Word for word. Including what he said, which I will not repeat aloud in the hall. It is on page four hundred and six if you want to look. Everybody has.
    - The record begins after the first winter. Of the winter itself, nothing; nobody knows why, and Ozzie has worn out three pairs of spectacles wondering. The first books that do survive are written on whatever the Walkers had: scavenged paper, ledgers turned upside down.
    - They are crumbling. Pages come away at the spine. I copy a page or two after every session, but the Table makes new arguments faster than I can save the old ones. One day I will open a volume and a joke will be gone that nobody alive remembers. That is what keeps me up.
    - I keep a private tally. Mid-speech changes of mind, Bastian Krell, twenty years: two hundred and twelve. Three in one sentence, once, about lamp oil. That was a good night.
    - Do not tell him about the tally. He would be proud of it, and then he would try to raise it, and I only have so much ink.
    - Go on, then. I will note that you visited. I note everything.
